blocks.h2: Will Your Old Gas Line Handle a New Appliance?
blocks.body: Skokie homes from the 1950s were piped for a furnace, a water heater, a range and maybe a dryer. Add a high-output range, a generator or a grill, and the original line may not deliver enough gas when everything runs at once. We add up the total load and check the pipe size from the meter. If needed, we upsize part of the line, so every appliance gets the gas it needs.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Installation Questions From Skokie Homeowners

items.q: Can I switch from an electric range to gas?
items.answer: Usually. We run a new branch to the kitchen and install a shutoff behind the range.

items.q: Can my old gas pipe handle a new appliance?
items.preview: We check the size and load first.
items.answer: We calculate the total load and check the size and condition of your existing pipe before connecting anything.
Yes, where the village requires one.

items.q: Can you run gas to my backyard grill?
items.answer: Yes. We run a protected line with a shutoff and a quick-connect at the grill.

items.q: What happens if a gas line is too small?
items.answer: Burners and heaters run weak or won't light properly when several appliances run at once.

items.q: How much does gas line installation cost in Skokie?
items.preview: It depends on the run. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the length of the run, the appliance and the route. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
